messages:

Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Request: Penetration test report & environment details for private VPC deployment

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call last week. As part of our procurement review we need a few items to close our security assessment for the Private deployment:

- A copy of the most recent penetration test report (redacted is fine) covering customer-facing surfaces when Redwood is deployed in a customer VPC.
- A short document describing the test scope/assumptions for VPC-hosted deployments (what is considered "in-scope" vs "out-of-scope").
- Evidence that critical findings identified in the last report were remediated, or a remediation plan with dates.

We also need to confirm whether external vendors (e.g., BlueShieldSec, the third-party firm listed in our intake) are permitted to run authenticated tests against our customer VPC during a scheduled window, and whether you will provide temporary test credentials or if we should use their own agent.

Can you send these artifacts or point us to a drive link? If redaction is required for sensitive items, please advise what you can share and what you will redact.

Appreciate it,
Elena Morris
Security Operations
FinServ Inc

[Attachment: finserv_pen_request_form.pdf (PDF)]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morris <security@finserv.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 10:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Penetration test report & environment details for private VPC deployment

Elena —

Thanks for the clear list. We can provide everything you asked for; below is what we will send and a couple clarifying questions so we scope what we share.

What we will provide (deliverables):
- Redacted pen test PDF that covers our private-deployment topology (attached).
- A compact scoping matrix that documents the boundary assumptions for Redwood in a customer VPC, including control-plane vs data-plane responsibilities and suggested test windows.
- Remediation tracker CSV summarizing critical and high findings, current status, and planned remediation dates.

Clarifications we need from you to avoid over/under-sharing:
1) Test target definition: do you want the pen test to include customer-managed components (e.g., your NAT gateways, customer-side SGs) or strictly Redwood-managed endpoints reachable over the peering/VPC connections? Our recommended default is: Redwood-managed endpoints only (Redwood control plane egress and model-serving endpoints) — customer-managed infrastructure is out of scope unless you explicitly request we coordinate with your infra team.
2) Authenticated testing model: we can provide short-lived service credentials scoped to the test window (recommended) or work with BlueShieldSec to run agentless external scans only. Which do you prefer?
3) Impact tolerance: confirm whether the test must be strictly non-disruptive (no destructive testing) or if low-risk exploitation simulations are permitted.

Attached is a preliminary scoping matrix (redwood_vpc_pen_scoping_matrix.xlsx) to capture these choices. If you confirm the three items above, we will finalize the redacted PDF and remediation tracker and share a Drive link.

Proposed next step: 30-minute alignment call with Elena, BlueShieldSec, Karthik (deployments), and Marissa (security engineer) — are you available Wed 5/6 at 11:00 PT?

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood_vpc_pen_scoping_matrix.xlsx (Excel)]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morris <security@finserv.com>, BlueShieldSec <ops@blueshieldsec.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Penetration test report & environment details for private VPC deployment

Elena / BlueShieldSec team —

Following up with the artifacts and a short summary of our assumptions. Attachments included: pen_report_redacted.pdf (redacted copy of our most recent independent assessment), remediation_tracker.csv (status for critical/high items), and the scoping matrix.

Boundary assumptions (concise):
- Customer-managed VPC: FinServ owns VPC networking, route tables, and customer-side security groups. Redwood services are deployed into customer subnets via our private control-plane integration and a service subnet we request be provisioned.
- In-scope (Redwood responsibility): model-serving endpoints, Redwood-managed inbound load balancers, control-plane egress to Redwood monitoring/telemetry endpoints, and any agent the customer installs that we maintain for telemetry.
- Out-of-scope (customer responsibility): customer-managed NAT, host-level access to customer-managed resources, and any third-party services FinServ connects to (unless explicitly arranged).
- Access model for pen tests: we are willing to provide short-lived, narrowly scoped credentials for authenticated tests against Redwood-managed endpoints inside the VPC. Credentials will be scoped to a specific role and will expire at the end of the agreed test window. We do not provide credentials that grant tenant-level administrative access to customer-managed infrastructure.
- Test window and impact: we require agreed windows and a non-disruptive testing agreement by default. Low-risk exploitation simulations may be permitted with prior approval; destructive or denial-of-service testing is not allowed unless explicitly negotiated and approved by our ops and customer teams.

If this fits FinServ's needs, please confirm and we will share a Drive link with the attachments and schedule the alignment call. If BlueShieldSec prefers to run unauthenticated external testing only, we can support that as well (but authenticated findings are generally higher fidelity).

Thanks — happy to jump on the call.

—
Lauren Bishop
Director, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- pen_report_redacted.pdf (PDF)
- remediation_tracker.csv (CSV)
- redwood_vpc_pen_scoping_matrix.xlsx (Excel)
